person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: null-result
span.quote: No striking relationship between frequency of experience and strength of set was revealed.

span.label: perceptual set induction with an ambiguous figure
span.quote: The present experiment deals with an attempt to observe the possible relation between the strength of a set and the frequency of set-inducing experiences.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: The experimental design involved presenting a varying number of setinducing experiences before testing with die ambiguous figure.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A PAPER DISOWNS THE TERM IN ITS OWN TITLE, AND SAYS WHICH TERM IT SHOULD HAVE BEEN: it appears appropriate to indicate that our findings **MIGHT HAVE MORE BEARING ON WHAT MIGHT BE TERMED “COGNITIVE” SETS RATHER THAN ON PERCEPTUAL SETS**. The article is titled “The Role of Frequency in Developing PERCEPTUAL Sets”, and the correction is made in the paper's own voice rather than left to a reader
span.quote: It appears appropriate to indicate tibat our findings might have more bearing on what might be termed "cognitive'' sets rather tiian on perceptual sets.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE DISOWNED WORD IS THEN RESERVED FOR A NARROWER CLASS, WITH AN EXAMPLE A READER CAN PICTURE: the term “perceptual” set **MIGHT BETTER BE RESERVED FOR** reference to those instances where a subject **IS LOOKING FOR OR EXPECTING TO SEE A SPECIFIC STIMULUS**, a friend's face in a crowd, for example. Having said the word does not fit their study, they say what it does fit - which is the harder half and the one usually skipped
span.quote: The term "perceptual" set might better be reserved for reference to those instances where a subject is looking for or expecting to see a specific stimulus, a friend's face in a crowd, for example

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE AMBIGUOUS STIMULUS IS DEFINED BY THE TWO CATEGORIES IT CAN FALL INTO, AND THE CATEGORIES ARE NAMED: it **CAN BE PERCEIVED AS BELONGING TO EITHER OF TWO COGNITIVE CATEGORIES OR CLASSES OR OBJECTS: ANIMALS AND HUMANS**. The figure's ambiguity is not a property of the drawing but of which of two named classes a viewer assigns it to
span.quote: It can be perceived as belonging to either of two cognitive categories or classes or objects: animals and humans.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A GAP IN THE PRIOR LITERATURE IS STATED AS A MISSING QUANTITY RATHER THAN A WRONG RESULT: while Leeper did find that he could control his subjects' responses by manipulating past experiences, he **DID NOT ATTEMPT TO DEMONSTRATE ANY SYSTEMATIC OR QUANTITATIVE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AMOUNT OF EXPERIENCE AND RESPONSE**. The predecessor is credited with the effect and the paper claims the function relating it to dose
span.quote: While Leeper did find that he could control his subjects' responses by manipulating past experiences, he did not attempt to demonstrate any systematic or quantitative relationship between amount of experience and response

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE INFERENCE FROM THE MEASUREMENT TO THE CONSTRUCT IS STATED AS A PRESUMPTION, IN THAT WORD: **THE PRESUMPTION HERE IS THAT** those with a strong set **WILL RESIST SUCH NEW SET INDUCTION MORE THAN** those with a weak set. What the experiment observes is resistance to a second induction; what it reports is strength of set, and the bridge between them is named a presumption by the authors
span.quote: The presumption here is that those with a strong set will resist such new set induction more than those with a weak set

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AND THE STRENGTH OF THE SET IS OPERATIONALISED BY BORROWING AN ASSUMPTION FROM A NAMED AUTHORITY: **ASSUMING, WITH ALLPORT,** that having different numbers of such experiences would result in different strengths of set, it was **ALSO DECIDED TO TEST FOR SUCH STRENGTH BY ATTEMPTING TO INDUCE THE ALTERNATE SET**. The premise is attributed rather than argued, and the test for the quantity is chosen after the premise is granted
span.quote: Assuming, with Allport, diat having different numbers of such experiences would result in different strengths of set, it was also decided to test for such strength by attempting to induce die alternate set

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE SCOPE OF THE WORD `PERCEPTION` IS LIMITED IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE METHOD IS DESCRIBED: although our experiment makes use of an ambiguous figure, **IT SHOULD BE CLEAR THAT WE ARE NOT SUGGESTING THAT THE STUDY IS DIRECTLY CONCERNED WITH PERCEPTION EXCEPT IN THE LIMITED SENSE OF PERCEPTION OF DIAGRAMMATIC PICTURES**. A disclaimer about what the central word covers, placed before the results rather than in a limitations section
span.quote: Although our experiment makes use of an ambiguous figure, it should be clear that we are not suggesting that die study is directly concerned with perception except in die limited sense of perception of diagrammatic pictures

span.label: The authors concede the procedure does not isolate frequency from other variables.
span.quote: While not completely free from the influence of other variables the procedure followed offers some observations on the strength of sets as a function of frequency.

span.label: Scope limit: the study bears on perception only in the narrow sense of perceiving diagrammatic pictures, not perception generally.
span.quote: Although our experiment makes use of an ambiguous figure, it should be clear that we are not suggesting that die study is directly concerned with perception except in die limited sense of perception of diagrammatic pictures (Gibson, 1951).

span.label: The null result may be specific to sets built on labels the subject already possesses; other kinds of set could still depend on frequency.
span.quote: It may be that other kinds of sets are much more regularly dependent upon the number of previous experiences but our data appear to support the conclusion that when previous experience has already prepared the subject with such labels as "animal" or "human," he can readily attach such labels to a specific situation very quickly.

span.label: past experience
span.quote: the construct of set has been used to demonstrate how we perceive or respond to a situation in terms of our past experience.

span.quote: No striking relationship between frequency of experience and strength of set was revealed.

span.label: perceptual sets
span.quote: The present results suggest that such perceptual sets are easily imposed, perhaps in a one-trial learning operation, and that they have an all or none quality at least over a short span of time.

span.label: one-trial learning
span.quote: The present results suggest that such perceptual sets are easily imposed, perhaps in a one-trial learning operation, and that they have an all or none quality at least over a short span of time.

span.label: label
span.quote: They may not have instructed themselves to label the pictures as members of a class until after they had seen several.

span.label: cognitive categories
span.quote: It can be perceived as belonging to either of two cognitive categories or classes or objects: animals and humans.

span.label: classes or objects
span.quote: It can be perceived as belonging to either of two cognitive categories or classes or objects: animals and humans.

span.label: animals and humans
span.quote: It can be perceived as belonging to either of two cognitive categories or classes or objects: animals and humans.

span.label: perceptual set - NARROWED BY THIS PAPER to looking for a SPECIFIC stimulus, with the example the authors chose to make it concrete: a friend's face in a crowd. The paper hands the term back with a smaller extension than its own title uses
span.quote: The term "perceptual" set might better be reserved for reference to those instances where a subject is looking for or expecting to see a specific stimulus, a friend's face in a crowd, for example, or a particular colour of book cover on a shelf.

span.label: cognitive set - a set to perceive a CLASS rather than a particular visual stimulus, argued from a case where the stimulus itself was ambiguous: a subject set for a B still reads a distorted figure as a B
span.quote: Even when the subjects are shown a series of letters or numbers with one of these distorted to appear as either a B or 13 as was done by Bruner and Minturn (1955), we cannot argue that the subjects were set to perceive that particular visual stimulus; they were cognitively set to perceive a B, or 13, regardless of its physical stimulus aspects.

span.label: ambiguous figure - not a property of the drawing but of WHICH OF TWO NAMED CLASSES a viewer assigns it to, with both classes stated: animals and humans THIS SPAN CARRIES THE FILE'S OCR DAMAGE, quoted verbatim because a quote is the staged file's bytes. The scan substitutes `th` with `di`/`ti` throughout - `die` for “the”, `diat` for “that”, `dien` for “then”, `tiian` for “than” - so the paper's sentence reads correctly and this transcription does not. Read rather than detected: there is no general detector, because `die` is also an English word. See Q-721.
span.quote: It can be perceived as belonging to either of two cognitive categories or classes or objects: animals and humans. Thus die figure can be seen as either a rat or an old man.

span.label: strength of a set - defined here only by the relation it is to be observed in: strength AS A FUNCTION OF the frequency of set-inducing experiences
span.quote: The present experiment deals with an attempt to observe the possible relation between the strength of a set and the frequency of set-inducing experiences.

span.label: a set that is BROKEN versus one that is REPLACED - the distinction the discussion substitutes for its own procedure's term, available only where a delay was interposed. `replaced` is used nowhere else in the paper, so it is a sense and not a node
span.quote: When a time factor is interposed it may be that the original set is not so much broken as replaced.

span.label: contradicts → Allport (1955), postulate that set strength increases with frequency of past experience
span.note: differs in: THE DISAGREEMENT IS SCOPED TO ONE KIND OF SET, BY THE AUTHORS. 'the present results offer ONLY LITTLE SUPPORT for the frequency proposition that Allport postulates, AT LEAST WITH RESPECT TO SUCH cognitive SETS.' `At least with respect to` is the authors bounding their own contradiction - it holds for cognitive sets and they decline to extend it. (Quote clipped before the paper's own quotation marks around `cognitive`, which are typographically irregular in the staged text - slice, do not retype.) Q-441.
span.quote: In general, then, the present results offer only little support for the frequency proposition that Allport postulates, at least with respect to such "cognitive'' sets.

span.label: extends → Leeper (1935)
span.quote: While Leeper did find that he could control his subjects' responses by manipulating past experiences, he did not attempt to demonstrate any systematic or quantitative relationship between amount of experience and response; he was more concerned with kind of experience, that is, whether the subjects were shown a simplified copy of the ambiguous figure with one of the interpretations emphasized or whether they were also told what to look for.

span.label: contradicts → Bruner and Minturn (1955), interpretation of the B/13 result as a perceptual set
span.note: differs in: PERCEPTUAL SET AGAINST COGNITIVE SET. 'EVEN WHEN the subjects are shown a series of letters or numbers with one of these distorted ... as was done by Bruner and Minturn (1955), WE CANNOT ARGUE THAT THE SUBJECTS WERE SET TO PERCEIVE THAT PARTICULAR VISUAL STIMULUS; they were COGNITIVELY SET to...' The disagreement with Bruner and Minturn turns on which kind of set the result demonstrates, not on the result. Q-441.
span.quote: Even when the subjects are shown a series of letters or numbers with one of these distorted to appear as either a B or 13 as was done by Bruner and Minturn (1955), we cannot argue that the subjects were set to perceive that particular visual stimulus; they were cognitively set to perceive a B, or 13, regardless of its physical stimulus aspects.

span.label: past experience —causes→ set
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — The paper's opening premise, and the half of it that its data confirm strongly: 75% of subjects follow a single prior picture.
span.quote: the construct of set has been used to demonstrate how we perceive or respond to a situation in terms of our past experience.

span.label: frequency of experience —causes→ strength of set
span.note: direction on the measure: no-change · strength of the relation: 0.15 — the record marks this weak — THE MEASURED ABSENCE OF THE RELATION THE EXPERIMENT WAS BUILT TO FIND, kept as an edge at weight 0.15 rather than omitted: an omitted edge records that the question was never asked. Pairs with `past experience -> set` at 0.9 - same paper, same procedure, prior exposure decides the response and MORE of it does not strengthen the set. That contrast is the paper's contribution and it is why claim_type is `null-result`.
span.quote: No striking relationship between frequency of experience and strength of set was revealed.

span.label: one-trial learning —causes→ perceptual sets
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — Offered by the authors as a suggestion - “perhaps in a one-trial learning operation” - and weighted for that hedge rather than against it.
span.quote: The present results suggest that such perceptual sets are easily imposed, perhaps in a one-trial learning operation, and that they have an all or none quality at least over a short span of time.

span.label: label —causes→ set
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — The authors' alternative to the frequency account: later responders were not slowly acquiring a set, they had not yet labelled the series as a class. THIS SPAN CARRIES THE FILE'S OCR DAMAGE, quoted verbatim because a quote is the staged file's bytes. The scan substitutes `th` with `di`/`ti` throughout - `die` for “the”, `diat` for “that”, `dien` for “then”, `tiian` for “than” - so the paper's sentence reads correctly and this transcription does not. Read rather than detected: there is no general detector, because `die` is also an English word. See Q-721.
span.quote: Adding more pictures does mean adding more people, but this does not necessarily mean that die later arrivals were slowly acquiring a set They may not have instructed themselves to label the pictures as members of a class until after they had seen several. Once the label had been attached, die set may have become operative in one trial.

span.label: cognitive categories —same-as→ classes or objects
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — A terminological equation the paper makes inline - “either of two cognitive categories or classes or objects” - rather than a relation between two constructs.
span.quote: It can be perceived as belonging to either of two cognitive categories or classes or objects: animals and humans.

span.label: animals and humans —is-a→ cognitive categories
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — Same span as the equation above, declared: the sentence both names the category pair and identifies its two members, which is what makes the figure's ambiguity checkable.
span.quote: It can be perceived as belonging to either of two cognitive categories or classes or objects: animals and humans.
